subject: Clarify: default log storage — what Redwood keeps and deletion options
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta@novaprocess.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick Q — what does Redwood keep by default?

Hi Rishi,

We're kicking off a technical review for our vendor sign-off and I need a concise summary of Redwood's default data capture for hosted API usage. Specifically:

- Do you store the full request payload (user prompt + metadata) by default?
- Are model outputs (generated answers/completions) treated the same as prompts for retention?
- For streaming responses or partial tokens (we stream on our side), do those fragments persist anywhere?
- What's the default retention period for stored items (requests, outputs, logs)?

We also need to understand options for limiting retention (shorter windows, on/off flags) and any EU residency controls — Novaprocess will have some EU users.

I've attached our standard SOC2 checklist; if you can return something short we can include in our security packet.

Thanks —
Marta Lopez
Security Operations
Novaprocess
[Attachment: SOC2_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@novaprocess.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what does Redwood keep by default?

Hi Marta — thanks for the checklist and the clear questions. High-level answers below; happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you'd like to walk through specifics for your integration.

Summary (hosted API defaults):
- Request payloads: by default we persist the full request payload (user prompt + any metadata you send) for 45 days. This is used for telemetry, billing, and quality/regression monitoring.
- Model outputs: generated outputs are stored and treated as captured artifacts and retained on the same default horizon (45 days) unless you enable auto-purge.
- Streaming fragments: transient streaming buffers (intermediate fragments before completion) are ephemeral — they are typically kept in a short-lived buffer for up to 24 hours and are not indexed as stored artifacts unless the request finalizes and an output object is created.
- Opt-outs & controls: you can set store=false on requests to opt out of persistent capture for specific calls. There are also org-level policies (for accounts) that can change defaults.
- EU residency: for Hosted we can pin residency to EU regions — data stored under an EU-residency flag remains in EU data stores and follows EU retention settings. Dedicated/Private deployments provide stronger residency guarantees.

Proof-of-deletion & audit: customers can request proof-of-deletion runs; for hosted accounts we surface deletion logs and a short runbook we follow.

Attached is a one-page retention summary I prepared for quick inclusion in vendor packets.

Next steps I propose:
1) If your default ask is a 7- or 30-day retention window, let me know which and whether EU residency is required (we have template language we can include in the MSA).
2) If you need org-level opt-out or guaranteed EU-only storage, we can discuss a Dedicated pilot (3 months) — Jonas is cc'd to scope technical options.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-retention-summary.pdf (pdf)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:41:00 -0800
Subject: Novaprocess asks — retention window & EU residency (internal)

Kimberly / Jonas — Novaprocess (contact: Marta Lopez) asked for a concise vendor statement and is pushing a procurement team that prefers a 7-day retention window for all captured artifacts and EU-only residency for EU users.

Questions / ask:
- Legal: can we commit in a standard SOW to a 7-day default retention for hosted customers, or do we need to route them to Dedicated/Private? What is our preferred contract language for an org-level retention override?
- Product: is 7-day hosted retention operationally feasible as an org-level setting, and would it have any logging/evidence gaps for billing/qa? If not, what is the minimum feasible hosted window without heavy infra work?

Suggested compromise for quicker close: offer a 30-day hosted retention with EU residency pin and an option to purchase Dedicated within the quarter for a tighter 7-day SLA. If that lands, we can expedite a procurement PO.

Marta indicated procurement will attach a PO once we confirm the retention/residency approach — I expect a quick decision if we can provide a clear path.

Thanks —
Rishi
From: Procurement <procurement@novaprocess.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta@novaprocess.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what does Redwood keep by default?

Hi Rishi — thanks for the clear summary. Novaprocess is comfortable moving forward on the basis below:

- Acceptance: 30-day default retention for request + outputs for hosted account, with EU-data pin for EU traffic.
- Action: Procurement attached our PO for an initial pilot (see attachment).
- Follow-up: we'll want a short SOW appendix to cover the residency guarantee and an expedited path to Dedicated if we need a 7-day retention SLA later.

Please confirm and send the draft appendix / SOW language for legal review. We can schedule a quick signature call once the appendix is in place.

Regards,
Novaprocess Procurement
[Attachment: Novaprocess_PO_4567.pdf (pdf)]
